title: The Spoon Holder's Opening Statement
title_candidates: Best in Field: From the Last Man You'd Expect
Mullin's Hot Stretch, Baker's Double Disaster
theme: The three-time Wooden Spoon holder opened with the best round in the field at one of the Open's most demanding links, while Alex Baker donated two back-nine catastrophes to his early cushion and the defending Trophy champion settled to last place before the fourth hole was done.
opening_hook: Open with the paradox: Mullin scores 40 Stableford points at Royal Cinque Ports, best in the field, from the man arriving with three consecutive Wooden Spoons — then move player by player through how the day unfolded.
foreshadow: Alex Baker leaks three consecutive doubles at H3-H5, an early sign of a concentration pattern that will detonate twice on the back nine.
Jon Baker, the defending Trophy champion, bogeys the par-3 4th (SI18 — the easiest hole on the course) to drop to last in the Wooden Spoon race; an omen dressed as a blip.

competition_state.name: Trophy
competition_state.note: Early jockeying was routine (Mullin drew level at H11); he took an outright lead at H16 — the same hole where Alex Baker was posting a quintuple — and held it. Baker's twin back-nine blowups (quad at H11, quintuple at H16) surrendered whatever gap might have closed.

competition_state.name: Green Jacket
competition_state.note: Baker (Alex) drew level at H6, Mullin retook the lead at H9; both exchanges were routine. Mullin led from H9 through the close, finishing 5 shots clear of Jon Baker.

competition_state.name: Wooden Spoon
competition_state.note: Baker (Jon) dropped to last at H4 with a bogey on SI18 and held that position for the remaining 14 holes, finishing 4 points behind Williams (33).

players.arc: Best in field with 40 Stableford points: a hot stretch H9-12 (birdie at the 10th plus three pars, 13 points across four holes) built the Trophy lead, with a double at the par-4 13th the only interruption before he secured it outright at H16.

Three consecutive doubles at H3-5 were the front-nine warning; the back nine collected the bill — quadruple at the par-4 11th (SI3, one of the hardest on the course) and quintuple at the par-5 16th, eight points surrendered in two holes, leaving him 3 behind Mullin at 37.

Dropped to last in the Wooden Spoon standings at H4 with a bogey on the easiest hole on the course (par 3, SI18) and never recovered: a back-nine run of three consecutive pars H11-13 (9 points) was too late and too little, closing on 29 points — last in the field.

Took a quadruple bogey at the par-5 3rd (SI4) early and recovered to post 33 Stableford points — third in the Trophy and 4 clear of Jon Baker in the Spoon standings; the day's stable presence in an otherwise volatile field.

venue_notes: Royal Cinque Ports is TEG's 2nd visit to this venue — a formidable championship links in Deal that has hosted two Open Championships, known for its exposed back nine and punishing rough. The second-visit context sharpens Mullin's 40-point round: the field had prior data on this course, and the reigning Spoon holder still led it.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker leaks three consecutive doubles at H3-H5, an early sign of a concentration pattern
payoffs.payoff: The front-nine leakage was the preview: Baker posted a quadruple at H11 (SI3) and a quintuple at H16, costing him 8 points in two holes and confirming the day's structural pattern.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker, the defending Trophy champion, bogeys the par-3 4th (SI18) to drop to last
payoffs.payoff: What looked like a blip at H4 proved to be the shape of the day: Baker's three pars H11-13 recovered ground but not enough, and he finished last at 29 points, 11 behind Mullin.
